audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition interest and earnings are absent from the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings anchor omits Kadant Profil earnings and incremental interest and taxes, while the bridge and shares represent the post-acquisition company.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect interest expense to increase significantly in 2026 as a result of the borrowing incurred in 2025 to fund our most recent acquisition and the anticipated borrowing in 2026 to fund our pending acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Kadant Profil cost $170.132 million and total obligations increased by $136.131 million from January 3 to July 4, amounts large relative to the $130.6 million anchor. Missing acquired earnings understates value, while missing financing costs overstates it; the filings do not establish the net effect.
audit_findings.action: Construct a normalized post-April 30 run rate including Kadant Profil owner earnings, incremental interest, taxes, integration costs and purchase-price adjustments, then rerun every scenario on a consistently dated bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-dependent growth may omit its economic reinvestment cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth enters the OE projection without an explicit deduction for acquisition consideration or another replacement-cost allowance for purchased growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect that a significant driver of our long-term growth will be the acquisition of businesses and technologies that complement or augment our existing products and services or may involve entry into a new process industry.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions are expected to be a significant growth driver and reports acquisition cash outlays of $300.335 million in 2024, $189.983 million in 2025 and $171.768 million in the first half of 2026. It also reports $28.295 million of 2025 intangible amortization. Whether that amortization was added back in the anchor and whether the 4% and 7% growth cases are strictly organic remain unresolved. Given the historical acquisition-spending scale, treating acquisition-dependent growth as free is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE workpaper for acquired-intangible amortization add-backs, document the organic growth support for each scenario, and deduct a recurring acquisition-cost or replacement-reinvestment allowance wherever acquisitions are required.

audit_findings.title: Seller-controlled purchase option is an unmodeled common-equity claim
audit_findings.mechanism: The future exercise payment belongs in the equity bridge, paired with the additional owner earnings attributable to the remaining subsidiary interest.
audit_findings.evidence: Under a put and purchase option as outlined in the securities purchase agreement, the seller can demand the Company purchase, or the Company can demand that the seller sell to the Company, the remaining interest in the subsidiary where the Company holds a noncontrolling interest at any time after December 31, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The seller's contractual right to compel a purchase after December 31, 2027 is demonstrated, but the exercise-price formula, affected subsidiary results and accounting classification are not quantified in the supplied record. The payment reduces value while the acquired minority earnings increase it, so neither net direction nor materiality can presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the purchase-agreement valuation formula, isolate the remaining subsidiary's 45% minority earnings and debt, estimate the exercise-date payment and present value, and rerun the bridge together with the incremental OE.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance-capital requirement may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.952-$9.952 million annual OE; computed $8.75-$14.64 per share reduction to bull value if the entire stated plan increase is maintenance
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalized maintenance capital reduces the OE anchor and therefore all forecast and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to make capital expenditures of approximately $23.0 to $27.0 million during 2026 for property, plant, and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The $17.048 million 2025 expenditure is demonstrably below the stated $23-$27 million 2026 plan, but the maintenance portion is unresolved. Even treating the entire $5.952-$9.952 million difference as additional annual maintenance would reduce the $203.39 bull value to approximately $188.75-$194.64 per share, still far below the $298.76 market price. That concrete upper-end comparison does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance, growth, integration and property-purchase capital expenditures across the enlarged perimeter and rerun OE using normalized maintenance capital.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be excess or readily distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $134.533 million maximum bridge exposure; $11.30 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating, restricted or non-distributable cash must be removed from the equity bridge cash add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents were $119.6 million at January 3, 2026, compared with $94.7 million at December 28, 2024, which included cash and cash equivalents held by our foreign subsidiaries of $100.3 million at January 3, 2026 and $73.8 million at December 28, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $134.533 million add-back is demonstrated, while its excess and distributable portion is unresolved. Removing the entire balance—more severe than any partial restriction—would reduce bull value from $203.39 to about $192.09 per share, still well below the $298.76 price. The issue can affect value but cannot change the present valuation conclusion at its maximum bridge exposure.
audit_findings.action: Determine unrestricted excess cash by jurisdiction at July 4, subtract minimum operating liquidity and restricted amounts, apply remittance costs or limitations, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.012 million recorded fair value ($0.17 per share); $12.140 million contractual maximum ($1.02 per share)
audit_findings.mechanism: The contingent purchase-price liability is a direct deduction from the equity bridge unless its cash payment is already included in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum future value of the contingent consideration subject to payment is approximately $11,711,000, calculated using the foreign currency spot rate at January 3, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the July 2026 filing records a $2.012 million liability and a $12.140 million maximum payment. Even the contractual maximum is only $1.02 per share versus the $95.37 gap between the $203.39 bull value and the $298.76 price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the July 2026 probability-weighted fair-value liability from equity value, confirm it is not already reflected in forecast cash flows, and show a sensitivity at the $12.140 million maximum.
